oliver-sample: FYI I hit another bundler parity footgun when trying to ship our JS sampleapp to the edge. Different manifest from the earlier issue: this one only shows up when code-splitting / dynamic-import is enabled.

maria-devex: Ugh, what happens?

oliver-sample: Repro summary: SDK ends up duplicated across two lazy chunks (one for runtime, one for page). Each chunk has its own module instance so our in-process token cache is split again -> 401 loops during cold start because each instance tries to refresh independently. Noticed only in browsers/edge-runtimes that do ESM dynamic import natively.

oliver-sample: Minimal repro:
1) TS app with route-based dynamic import: `const { createClient } = await import('redwood-inference-sdk')` in routes/routeA.tsx and again in routes/routeB.tsx.
2) Build with webpack/rollup/vite default split/chunk settings.
3) Run in edge worker harness -> both chunks load, both execute SDK init -> two caches.

jonathan-bundler: Logs we saw in the harness: `AuthError: token expired` repeated, then `RateLimitError: too many auth attempts`. Found two copies of `redwood-inference-sdk` in the generated asset manifest (hashes differ).

sunita-sdk: Sounds similar root cause to duplicate-resolve, but triggered by dynamic import + chunking. Does the package have multiple entry files or conditional exports?

oliver-sample: SDK's package.json has `exports` map (./dist/index.mjs and ./dist/index.cjs). The bundler sometimes resolves one chunk to the mjs path and another chunk to the package root which maps differently, so the resolver thinks they are different modules.

maria-devex: Workarounds that helped me: 
- Webpack: set `optimization.splitChunks.cacheGroups` to force shared vendor bundle for redwood-inference-sdk. Example: `test: /[\/]node_modules[\/]redwood-inference-sdk[\/]/, name: 'vendor-sdk', chunks: 'all', enforce: true`
- Rollup/Vite: set `build.rollupOptions.output.manualChunks` to group the SDK into one chunk or use `inlineDynamicImports: true` for small sample apps.
- Vite: also `resolve.dedupe: ['redwood-inference-sdk']` and `ssr.noExternal: ['redwood-inference-sdk']` for SSR/edge builds.

jonathan-bundler: Another option: use `preserveEntrySignatures: 'strict'` and consistent `mainFields` ordering so both static and dynamic import paths resolve identically.

sunita-sdk: Thanks, this is actionable. On the SDK side we can try: 
- Make a tiny single-file ESM entry that re-exports everything from dist and ensure `exports` points to it for the `import` condition. That reduces path divergence.
- Add an idempotent runtime guard: `if ((globalThis as any).__REDWOOD_SDK_INSTANCE) { module.exports = globalThis.__REDWOOD_SDK_INSTANCE } else { globalThis.__REDWOOD_SDK_INSTANCE = exports }` — to avoid multiple caches. (We prefer not to, but it's a pragmatic guard for edge bundles.)

oliver-sample: CI: build/edge-sample/4738 failed with the chunked build. Snippet: `manifest.json contains vendor-sdk.[hash].js and vendor-sdk2.[hash].js (both include redwood-inference-sdk)`.

ci-bot: build/edge-sample/4738 failed on linux-arm64 - logs: https://ci.internal/reports/4738

maria-devex: Action items: 1) devex will add the route-dynamic-import sample and webpack/vite/rollup configs demonstrating the split-chunk repro (PR queued). 2) SDK (sunita): please evaluate making a single thin ESM re-export entry and consider the guarded global dedupe as a last resort. 3) Docs: add a short note in the edge onboarding about chunk dedupe & recommended bundler flags.

sunita-sdk: Will create a small PR to add a canonical `exports` ESM entry and run the sampleapp CI. If that doesn't fully fix it we'll consider the runtime guard but would prefer a packaging fix first.

maria-devex: Great, thanks. Tagging @jonathan-bundler to help with manifest checks in CI once PRs land. :v:
